title: Complete source-defined concentration stocks stop at a generic no-proposal disposition
independence: Reviewer did not author the worker decisions, proposals or source captures. Source captures are author-collected primary evidence; their original authorship and retrieval timestamps are retained.
scope: Nine frozen case decisions representing seven source-qualified preparations. This is not a demand to mint every stock, approval of any owner, or a finding against a final published head.
description: Each selected decision records a recovered source formulation, no proposal, no missing requirement, and the same future-integration no-change text. Avoiding dry-solute or generic-stock equivalence is correct, but does not itself explain why the authorized proposal stage should stop once a source-qualified preparation is established. Exact next steps or a concrete unresolved identity/ownership requirement are missing.

requested_resolution: For each bounded source-qualified preparation, produce a native-schema-valid proposal with exact source/formulation/component provenance and proposed identity scope, or state the specific scientific/ownership requirement that prevents it.
Consolidate the two pairs of long/short labels only within their verified NBRC1339 source context; do not promote unqualified global stock aliases.
Preserve source water-addition quantities, preparation endpoints, component form limits and final-volume uncertainty; do not infer a dry hydration state from stock molarity.
Resolve cross-worker or existing-owner duplication before integration; an explicit owner conflict is a legitimate blocker, unlike generic future-work wording.
Run proposal validation and independent scientific review before any integration, support promotion, or release.
limitations: Only the nine listed frozen decisions are the confirmed finding; no global claim that all held stocks are resolvable.
The worker was still revising the shard when the snapshot was captured.
No current GitHub deduplication or issue mutation was performed by this reviewer.
Existing canary issue 1159 concerns different artifact corrections; this finding is not a request to broaden it.
